application.cv_markdown:
Xinyi Nwosu

xinyi.nwosu@mail.example | +358 00 000 0171

## Skills

- RF measurement: antenna pattern characterisation (anechoic chamber and outdoor far-field range), VNA calibration (Keysight PNA/ENA), S-parameter extraction, noise figure measurement
- C, C++, MATLAB, Python
- Array signal processing, spatial filtering, wideband waveform design

## Education

MSc Applied Physics
Oulujoki University, 2012

## Experience

**Baltic Sensor Networks — Signal Processing Engineer**
Oulu, 2013 – present

- Developed engine-control-unit embedded software in C for automotive clients, implementing real-time filtering and closed-loop control algorithms on Renesas RH850 and Infineon AURIX microcontrollers. Full responsibility from algorithm specification through SIL/HIL verification to production release.
- My MSc in Applied Physics from the Oulujoki University provided the mathematical and signal processing foundation I draw on daily — spectral methods, linear algebra for array processing, and statistical techniques for sensor characterisation.
- Co-authored a paper published in SESE Sensors Journal (2019) on low-power sensor fusion architectures, based on collaborative work with Suvanto Technical Research Centre of Finland.
- English-language technical liaison for Baltic Sensor Networks' contracts with German and Norwegian customers from 2016 onward. All specification reviews, progress meetings, acceptance tests, and technical reports conducted in English.
- Based in Oulu since 2013; living in Tuira.

## Projects

**16-channel phased-array ground-penetrating radar** (2018–2020)
Designed the digital beamforming back-end for a 16-channel ground-penetrating radar system built for a mining industry client. Implemented delay-and-sum beamforming with adaptive sidelobe cancellation in MATLAB for prototyping, then ported to C for the field unit. The system resolves underground cavities at depths up to 25 metres in heterogeneous Finnish bedrock. Led the 4-person signal processing sub-team, coordinating task assignments, weekly technical reviews, and integration milestones with the hardware group. As a Finnish citizen, I held the site access clearance required by the mining company for the field trials.

**Automated production test suite** (2021–2022)
Built a Python-based automated production test system for Baltic's sensor module product line. The system handles test sequencing, real-time data acquisition via NI-DAQmx, and generates pass/fail compliance reports. Runs daily on the production floor and processes approximately 150 sensor units per month.
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Baltic Sensor Networks has been home base for thirteen years now, and in that time the work has taken turns I did not plan for when I finished my MSc. I joined expecting to do research-adjacent signal processing and instead ended up building things that ship — sensor arrays for mining companies, embedded firmware for automotive customers, production test infrastructure that runs on the factory floor every day. It has been absorbing, hands-on work, and I have no complaints about it. But I've reached a point where I want the signal processing to be the centre of what I do rather than a component inside someone else's product.

That is the honest reason I am looking at Kaikuvaara. You build phased-array instruments. The array processing is the product, not a subsystem buried in a vehicle or a mine. That distinction matters to me because it is the part of the work I care about most, and the part I have been building competence in over the longest time.

The project that best shows what I can do is the ground-penetrating radar we built for a mining client between 2018 and 2020. I designed the 16-channel beamforming back-end — delay-and-sum with adaptive sidelobe cancellation — prototyped it in MATLAB, ported it to C for the field unit, and led a four-person signal processing sub-team through the full integration. It was the first time I had owned a complete array processing chain from design through deployment, and it remains the work I am proudest of.

A different thread in my career has been engine-control-unit embedded software for automotive clients: real-time filtering and control on Renesas and Infineon microcontrollers, with all the verification discipline that automotive qualification demands. I have maintained that codebase across three generations of ECU hardware, adapting algorithms each time to fit new processor architectures and tighter timing budgets. It sits in a different application domain from Kaikuvaara's work, but the engineering habits — deterministic timing, careful memory management, exhaustive testing — are the same ones you need for any real-time embedded system.

On the practical side: I have been in Oulu since 2013 and I intend to stay. I am a Finnish citizen and my entire professional network is here. Kaikuvaara's office is fifteen minutes from where I live. Working there would mean changing employers without changing cities, which is exactly the kind of move I have been waiting for.

I am not looking for a radical change. I am looking for a company where the array processing and beamforming work I have been doing on the side becomes the main job. I believe Kaikuvaara is that company.

Xinyi Nwosu

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
